Silius Italicus, the author of the Punica; and that Nero perished during his consulship is confirmed both by other authorities and by Martial himself, who indicates as much in those verses about Silius:^r After he had governed the mighty year with its twice-six fasces — he who was hallowed when the world had been set free — he devoted his remaining years to the Muses and to Phoebus, and now frequents Helicon in place of his own forum.

While Nero held supreme power — and indeed, as most hold, toward the end of his reign — Paul wrote that epistle in which Pudens, Linus, and Claudia send their greetings to Timothy. But there will be occasion to speak of these again in the third chapter.
